 by Ray Kuhn October 28, 2026 written by Ray Kuhn October 28, 2026 20 Now we get to see what they are made of. There are multiple Week 2 fantasy basketball rookies to watch, and we'll break it all down for you. Each week, we'll walk through the top-5 across points, rebounds, assists, three-pointers, steals, and blocks as well as the performance of the week. It might not be the best game for a rookie over the past seven days, but it's going to be one that's noteworthy and caught my attention. While there won't always be surprises across the top-5, it will guide our thought process as well as provide a glimpse into fantasy value. When it comes to steals, blocks, and three-pointers, this is especially true as it could present some fantasy basketball rookies to target.
 A lot of the names below, Caleb Wilson, Cameron Boozer, Keaton Wagler, and Darius Acuff Jr shouldn't be a surprise. As he works off the rust, I'd expect to see a lot more of Mikel Brown, Jr as he's shown flashes of success when given the chance. The biggest problem here, is just building up his stamina and getting past his minute restriction.
 AJ Dybantsa hasn't played yet this season as he nurses an ankle injury, but his debut is quite imminent; potentially on Wednesday. The biggest problem for Darryn Peterson has been his 36% shooting from the field as, in 30 minutes per game, he is getting an opportunity. We are far from sounding any alarms here.
 Please note that all stats are entering play Tuesday, October 27th.

 Rookie Performance of the Week
 Yaxel Lendeborg, Golden State Warriors
 10/26 @ Denver Nuggets - 31 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists 
 Get used to seeing a lot of the 11th overall pick in this space. Yes, we are just four games into Lendeborg's professional career, but he's taken his starting role in Golden State and is running with it. The performance above highlighted the fact that he's a complete player who will get every opportunity to succeed  this season.
 Top 5 Rookie Point Leaders
 Cameron Boozer continues to struggle with efficiency as he's shooting just 28.3% from the field through four games. He'd be a lot higher on this list even if he shot 40%, as the forward has also been partially saved by his five free-throw attempts per game. The fact that he's shooting 94.7% from the foul line also helps. The Grizzlies drafted Boozer for more than just his scoring, but he's taken 60 shots through four games. Once he improves his shooting, Boozer could be the most complete player in this draft class.

 Top 5 Rookie Rebound Leaders
 The ankle injury to Cameron Johnson means that Denver's second-round pick will take on a larger role early in the season. When given the chance, Trevon Brazile has produced through his first three games of the season. With the playing time expected to continue, Brazile could be an unexpected source of rebounds.

 Top 5 Rookie Assist Leaders
 To this point, none of the rookies have truly emerged as distributors. Darius Acuff Jr does have our attention as there were some questions throughout the draft process as to how well he'd do anything but score. The Sacramento Kings have no reason not to trust Acuff, and to this point, he's proving them correct. He's also going to be linked to Keaton Wagler and Brown for the duration of their careers.

 There are no surprises at the top of the list, but seeing Brazile contribute, in addition to his rebounds, is a pleasant development. Emanuel Sharp is averaging about 15 minutes per game, but until that rises, it will be difficult to truly count on him. Additionally, there's nothing to suggest Sharp will receive more playing time.

 Top 5 Rookie Block Leaders
 The depth of the Oklahoma City Thunder has already been attacked with injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Mara was drafted in the first round, but given his size (7'3") and skill set, so he's going to be limited to being the backup center. However, with Chet Holmgren now dealing with a knee injury, the Thunder's hand might be forced. If it leads to more blocked shots from Mara, it might not be a bad thing.
